utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I just had a quick order of business before we deal with the next witness, which my colleague will be doing. I just wanted to indicate that with respect to the decision of this Chamber on the 2nd of July of this year, and that was the decision that related to exhibits that the Prosecution added to its exhibit list from the two RFAs, 1755, 1756, the Chamber had asked the Prosecution to notify the Chamber once the English translations were available and once those had been uploaded into e-court. I can indicate that I've been advised that they are now available, that all of those English translations are now available, and that they have been uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If that is the case then there is no reason why they should not be included into the exhibit and it be identified as an exhibit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sorry, that they be identified as ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That they -- we will worry about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's a lady waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon to those in Pristina. We are ready to hear the evidence of a witness whom we will call K58. Is what I am saying being translated to the witness? I see nodding of agreement. Could the witness please read the affirmation on the card that is now given to her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be speaking closer to the microphone because we didn't hear her very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. I have heard enough to indicate that the witness did read the affirmation. If she sits she will be closer to the microphone. So could the witness -- could you please sit down now. Thank you. Now, there are going to be some questions for you, and I will ask Ms. D'Ascoli to commence with those questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I will begin by showing you a document which contains some personal information related to you. This is the 65 ter number 02477.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Please do not put it on the screen because it will be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you just read it for yourself and could you confirm whether the information in this document, meaning your name, your date and place of birth is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You now tender that under seal, do you?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01078 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, I will be referring to you as K58 in order to protect your identity. K58, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in February 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And before appearing for testimony today, have you had the opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the information contained in this statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, everything is true and correct. I have shown what I saw with my eyes and what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender the witness statement and it is the 65 ter number 02473, which is the unredacted version to be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01079, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Your Honours, I should point out that the date of birth indicated in the statement is inaccurate, is not correct, while the correct one is the one indicated in the attestation by the Presiding Officer pursuant to Rule 92 bis which is at the beginning of the English version of the statement and is -- also the correct one is also the one reflected into the pseudonym sheet that I've just tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: There is also a redacted version of the witness statement to be tendered as a public exhibit and this is the 65 ter number 02550, and I would seek to tender this too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01080, public.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: K58, did you also testify before this Tribunal in the Milutinovic et al. case in November 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you recently have the opportunity to review your previous testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And having reviewed this testimony, if today you were asked the same questions would you provide substantially the same answers and testify in the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. It's 11 years now since that time. Maybe I have forgotten something, but I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender also the transcript into evidence. This is 65 ter number 05091.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that need to be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01081.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I can now provide a brief summary of this witness's evidence. The witness is from the Decani municipality and describes the attack by Serb forces on the village of Beleg, in the Decani municipality, on or about 28th of March, 1999. She describes those forces and the shelling and shootings all around the village. The witness, together with approximately 100 other persons, was forced by policemen and paramilitaries out of the house where they were staying in Beleg. He she witnessed men being shot and beaten up. The witness reports that men and women were separated in the yard of the house. They were then taken in groups of four or five to the basement of the house, where they were all searched for money and other personal belongings. The women were then put in two rooms of a house for the night. During the night, the witness saw that Serb forces took some young girls out of the room and heard one girl telling her mother that she had been raped. The following day, all the villagers were ordered to go to Albania. The witness travelled on a lorry. They drove through a number of villages before arriving to Kukes on the Albanian border. En route they were stopped a number of times by Serb forces and asked for their identity documents and passports. Many men were at that point missing and never came back, amongst them the witness's husband. And this is the end of the in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: K58, as you know, the Chamber already has before it your previous testimony and your statement. Therefore, I'll just have a few questions for you today just to clarify some parts of your evidence. At page 3 of your statement, in both the English and the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And for the record -- for the English version I'm not referring to the numbering of pages in e-court, but to the actual number of pages in the statement, so that both versions are -- have the same numbering.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- so at page 3 of your statement, last paragraph, you say that you were approximately 100 people taking shelter in Nezir Vishaj's house in the village of Beleg. Can you tell us who these 100 people were, K58?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were civilians, children, elderly people, women, all of them were civilians. We were there because there was shelling all day long. We were staying at Naim Vishaj's house, all of us staying in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you tell us the ethnicity of these 100 people who were with you there in Nezir Vishaj's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were Albanian, all of them. We were all Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And could you briefly describe the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Children, elderly people, women, civilians, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. And can you please describe the conditions in the house in those days that you spent there with these other people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: We all were staying in one room. Shelling was going on all day. We didn't dare go out even to the yard. We were all staying in that room. We were staying at Naim's house. On the next day the policemen came.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- thank you for that. When describing how all these people were forced out of Vishaj's house, you mentioned that you saw Naim Vishaj being taken to a shed by a policeman. This is at page 4 of the statement for the record. Did you ever see Naim --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- Vishaj again after that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. They came into the yard, the Serb police, and forced Naim to order all of us to leave the house. And they shot 2 metres away from me, Nezir Vishaj, they shot him on his cheek. Then after him, Daut Alickaj was the second who was shot dead. And I saw him when he fell down on the ground --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Madam --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- I saw the police taking away Naim Vishaj and took him to the shed, cow-shed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And after that moment, did you ever see him again or is he alive to date, Naim Vishaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him anymore. But I heard from his wife, she said, I heard fire-arms and they had killed him. But I didn't eye-witness his death. But I know from his wife that he was shot dead because she had heard the shots. I had my children. I didn't want to have anything to do with others. I was worried about my own children.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Madam, in your statement, this is still at page 4, you say that you were taken to a basement of a house where there were already about 20 people. Can you tell me by whom were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. The policemen came and took us out of Naim's house and took us to another house, to a basement. There were some elderly people, they were paralyzed, they couldn't walk, and they were beating that old man with a stick. And I heard his daughter telling the policeman, He is paralyzed, he can't walk. And they shot at him. Then they took us to a basement where there were some 20 persons from all over the village of Beleg; they had been taken there.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And again, which were -- which was the ethnicity of these other 20 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Albanians, Albanians. They had taken them in -- from other houses, like they did with us but before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: All of them were civilians, all elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Madam, you mentioned that it was the police who took you there. Did you also see other forces around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. They were mixed. Some were policemen, some were paramilitaries. They wore two sorts of uniforms, paramilitaries -- I don't know how to say it because a long time has passed and I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just tell us what these other -- what the paramilitaries were doing at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They took us, all of us, to that basement. When the basement was full of people --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Was the -- excuse me, Madam --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- they took us out of it to a large meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I was just asking you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They kept there until dusk.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I was just asking you -- because you mentioned that the policemen came and took you out of Naim's house and to this other house to the basement, and I was just asking you what the paramilitaries were doing at that moment, if you remember, given that you mentioned these other forces as well together with the policemen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They took us from that house to that basement that I mentioned. All of us were gathered in the basement. After that, they took us out from the basement and took us to a meadow, and we were together in that meadow, men, women, children. Then they started to separate men from women --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Just a second, Madam. So were the paramilitaries operating together with the policemen? This is what understand from your answer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, yes, together. They were -- all the time they were working together.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And, Madam, at page 5 of your statement you say that you were also checked together with other three women, and you already described this in your testimony in the Milutinovic case. This for the record is at pages 7488 to 7490. What I wanted to ask you, Madam, is what you saw on the white piece of cloth --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- that you mentioned in your previous testimony in the Milutinovic transcript. And this is pages 7491 to 7492 -- if you can tell us which type of objects or items you saw on that cloth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They checked the men first --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, we have that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- they started with the men --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you just hear my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Then they continued with us, women. They took us four by four or four by five --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Madam, excuse me. Did you hear my question? I was asking you in particular with regard to the piece of cloth that you mentioned in your previous testimony and I was asking you if you could describe to us what you saw on that piece of cloth when you were in the basement to be checked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: You mean the policemen? They had some insignia which said "milicija."

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No. I think there's a problem with the translation. I was referring to the moment in which you were taken to the basement together with three other women to be checked. And when you testified some time ago in the Milutinovic -- please, just listen to my question and then reply. Thanks. When you testified before, you say -- you said that when you were brought to the basement to be checked you saw a piece of cloth lying on the floor, where you saw like many objects. And I was just asking you if you can describe to us what you saw on that piece of cloth. That was all -- in my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Now I understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: When we entered that basement to be checked, there was a white piece of cloth, and on that there was money, there were IDs. When I entered there, I handed over of my own free will whatever I had on me because I didn't want them to check me, to search me.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Seeing that there were such objects on that piece of sheet, I did the same, and then I went out and the other three women were there to be checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Madam, you mentioned IDs. Could you give us an approximate number of how many there were, if it was few or many, just an approximation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Approximately, because I didn't of course count them, I would say there were about 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And was your ID taken away or did you give away your ID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I didn't have my ID on me because it was burned. When my house took fire, my ID was burned, so I didn't have any. But those who had theirs were taken -- were deprived of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you see that yourself? Did you see that other people had to give away their IDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the IDs on that piece of sheet that I mentioned and there were people there before me, so that's why I thought. There were money -- there was money, jewellery, IDs on that piece of sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Madam, at page 6 of your statement you mention Mushk Jakupi's son as one of those who would come and pick up young girls in the room where you were staying during the night. Now, can you tell us how you could recognise him and how many times you saw him during that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I recognised Mushk Jakupi's son when the police came and took us to that meadow, and he was on a tank and my husband told me -- he recognised him first and he said to me, This is Mushk Jakupi's son. And then I looked at him and I could see that it was him --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- and he would turn the tank towards us or towards another group sometimes. He didn't want us to look at him, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Madam, do you remember you also mentioned having seen him during the night in which you were staying in a room of a building of a house and when you saw people coming in and taking young girls to -- for cleaning, in your statement you also mention having seen Mushk Jakupi's son in that occasion. So I was asking you, if you could clarify for us, how could you see him or when or how many times you saw him during that night? I understand how you could recognise him because it was your husband pointing his name to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. During the night it was dark, of course, but they had torches. There was several times that they came, but once -- on one occasion the torch light fell on him and that's when I saw him and I remembered that I saw him during the day as well. And I assumed it was the same person at night.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. So during the night you say it was on one occasion. Is it correct, was it only on one occasion that you saw him during that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Just once.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I just saw him once. I couldn't tell you how many times he was there before because --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No problem, that's fine, Madam. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- it was only on that occasion that the torch light fell on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, let's move to the moment when you were told by Serb forces to go to Albania and you started moving towards the Albanian border. And for the record, this is at page 7 of the statement. Madam, can you describe this convoy in which you were, how you were moving towards Albania, and if, for example, you can tell us how many people were on the move to Albania and what was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The next day around 9.00 they came and told us to leave and go towards Albania -- to go to Albania because we had asked for NATO to come and help us. All of us were Albanian, women, children, disabled people --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- and elderly. Everybody was civilian. All of us were civilians. And they forced us to go to Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And you say that "they came and told us to leave." Can you specify who do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The police, the police and military. They were mixed. They came in the morning and told us to go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And -- yes, can you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: We couldn't look at them. We were so afraid to even look at them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you also -- could you give us an approximation of how many of us, how many villagers, Albanians, as you said -- sorry, women, children, disabled persons, Kosovo Albanians, how many were you like on the move towards Albania --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're asking over the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I couldn't hear --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were so many people. There were about 200 or 300 people. I couldn't count them. There were many.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And, K58, my last question, at page 7 of your statement there is a list of names of missing persons, persons you knew of. Can I ask you if they're still missing to date and where were these people from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Sixty-six men went missing in Beleg and I all knew -- I knew all of them, especially the ones that I mention in my statement Arif Mazrekaj, his son Jetmir Mazrekaj, Sahit Mazrekaj, Hasan Mazrekaj, Hajdar Mazrekaj, Neke Binakaj, Mehmet Tolaj; I knew all of them. There were 66 men from the village; they are still missing and we don't know where their graves are, where they have been buried. We don't have their bodies to bury them again properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And what about your husband, did he have the same fate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: My husband is on the same list. He's still missing. He's the 66th person on that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Madam, given that in your statement there's a shorter list which of course doesn't include all these 66 men, do I understand you correctly that all the persons listed in your statement are also still missing and that they were from Beleg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: These people that are still missing are from Drenoc that I have included in -- on this list. But the others are from Sllup, Beleg, Carrabreg. I did not know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The ones that I knew are on the list that is included in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Madam. I don't have any further questions for you and thank you for having answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have further questions for the witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now there will be some further questions for you. This will be Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask - and you have a written submission - for Madam O'Leary to do the cross-examination. Thank you very much for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The next questions will be asked by a lady, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, K58. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have a great deal of questions, but I do want to clarify a few things, in particular with your statement that you gave in February of 2000. When you gave that statement in February of 2000, were other people present at that time other than those representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. But this statement was taken in February of 2000, so it was within a year of the time of the events you're speaking of; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I think that's correct, but I'm sorry I have forgotten the dates and this is because of the traumas we suffered during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall when you finished giving the statement that it was read back to you in Albanian, and then you signed as being a true recollection of the events; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then you were visited again by the Office of the Prosecutor on 9 September 2004; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I apologise again because I can't remember the dates. There have been many people who came to us and I've forgotten how many of them. Even if you ask me the birthdays of my children now maybe I wouldn't be able to tell you all of them. There were so many people who came and asked us questions and took statements. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. And specific dates aren't as important, but I'm basically wondering if you had a chance to review your statement in 2004 in anticipation of testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: You mean now?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: No, in September 2004 you would have first seen probably an Albanian version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I don't know. I apologise again. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could have P1079.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If you could look at that exhibit actually. And I believe in the English version and perhaps on the Albanian version on the first page, there's a signed declaration actually. If you could take a quick look at that at the very beginning of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at that time you corrected your birth date; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then do you recall after that time reading through it that a couple of years later, right before you testified in the Milutinovic trial, you again met via videolink to review your statement with some people from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I apologise, I can't remember. The only thing I remember is that the date of birth was wrong and that's it. I can tell you about the things that happened to me during the war, everything about that, but I can't remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Then maybe let's look at how many times you've appeared via videolink or you've dealt with videolink. At least twice you testified in the trial of Milutinovic et al., correct, via videolink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: This is the second time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. And before each of these times of testifying, you had a meeting via videolink with the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: You mean this time?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I actually mean both times, but yes once was last week on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. I think so. I'm not a hundred per cent sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And both of those times you had some changes to make, slight changes, to your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: It's been 11 years. I'm sorry I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I understand about 11 years, but I'm actually just asking about last week. You had approximately ten changes to your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, but I don't remember we had changes, and today I didn't go through any changes with the witness besides the birth date. What was contained in the supplemental information sheet was information or issues that we discussed, but it wasn't changes to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour, but I would suggest that the Defence sees that what she has stated in her supplemental information sheet that we'll put to her are actually changes and modifications to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Proceed, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So -- okay. Thank you very much. We'll go through them one by one and see if they're amendments to your statement or just rather clarifications, just to clear a few things up if that's okay. The first one that was discussed in your supplemental information sheet -- and if you want to see it we have it available. Unfortunately it's only in English, but I can read to you the relevant portions. It would be D004-2832 as document number. But in regard to some of the supplemental information notes that you had, you stated that by "Serb forces" you mentioned you meant "policemen." And this is in regard to your statement page 2 of the English version, paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, but it might not be easy for the witness to understand the references to page and paragraph. So maybe just for the sake of completeness if you could identify -- if my learned colleague could identify more specifically the piece of evidence she is referring to in the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, if we look at page 2 in the English, I believe page 2 in the Albanian as well of your statement, and this is P1079, and if it's not broadcast because that is the unredacted version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest you read the passage in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then read what you have that has been put to you as the additional information.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And see then whether the witness will confirm that they're different and why.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So I'm reading from page 2 of the English and it says: "I fled my village because the Serb forces were positioned in our village ..." And now at this time we received a supplemental information sheet that says: "The Serb forces she mentions in this paragraph were policemen ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were Serb policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But before you said just "forces." Do you differentiate to say "policemen"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The Serb police and military forces were the ones that forced us to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you describe to me what you mean by "policemen" when you use the word "policemen," ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were wearing regular police uniforms and they had "police" written on their arms. We were in so much stress and traumatised at the time, we couldn't look at them properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what colour were the uniforms that you would identify with the policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The usual that the police wear. They were blue camouflage. I don't know how else to describe them. The regular uniforms worn by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you remember testifying in Milutinovic et al. and describing the police uniforms as one solid colour, like a greyish colour, the usual uniforms police wore. They had written on their arms "police" in Serbian Cyrillic letters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were solid colour and the letters were Cyrillic, yes. But they were police uniforms, and I saw the Cyrillic letters on the arm. We couldn't buy those kinds of uniforms, and we couldn't see --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We couldn't see the uniforms in great details in the kind of situation we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What do you mean by "we couldn't buy those kinds of uniforms," who couldn't buy those kinds of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I meant we couldn't look at them properly in detail what kind of uniforms they were because we didn't dare to look at them in the eye. We didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So would you say at this time, though, ma'am, that the police uniforms were camouflage or one solid colour like greyish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The policemen were wearing solid-colour uniforms. The other ones had camouflage uniforms with patterns. Some of them were green with patterns. The policemen had solid-colour uniforms. But as I told you, I was worried about my children. I couldn't just look in detail what kinds of uniforms that were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And just a second ago you said "the other ones had camouflage uniforms with patterns." Who were the "other ones"?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Could I ask my learned colleague to clarify a bit -- being more specific with the witness. Because you start off my talking -- by referring to a paragraph which in the statement refers to sixth months before the events, and now we are going I think into the year 1999 -- I mean, I'm not sure. It's just that the witness could be confused if you don't clarify when she saw which type of uniforms. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And specifically I was going to get to when she specifically saw which ones. I was just looking for a range of uniforms the police had as far as she was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You described an insignia that you had seen on the arms of the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They had insignia there. I don't know exactly what they -- what the letters said. They were Cyrillic. I could only assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, can we look possibly then at P327.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, ma'am on that first page --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Approximately it resembles this one and this one, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you say "approximately," you're looking at the first page of P327; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: There is a book here in front of me, number 5 and number 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you saw both number 5 and number 7. When did you see number 5 and number 7?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I can remember the insignia a little bit. They were on the arm there. I can remember the Cyrillic letters, but what the whole word said, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When did you see number 5, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: 1999, when the police forces entered Naim's house and took us from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when did you see number 7, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I think it was on the same day. I wouldn't be sure. I'm only speaking approximately, but I think it was on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you look at page 2 and tell me if you've ever seen any of the insignias on page 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I can't remember these ones. I only remember the letters on the arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you testified previous in Milutinovic at T7477 and 7478 that you know some Cyrillic words; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Not words but the letters. I can recognise them that they are Cyrillic. I know that the letters are Cyrillic. For example, the ones I can see here now are in Cyrillic, but I don't know what the word says.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, in Milutinovic et al. you were asked specifically about the arm badge insignia and you said: "I have an eight-year education. We know some Serbian language. I know some Cyrillic words. I can discern them. I cannot understand, and I cannot speak."

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't receive a translation on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Please, I want to say this. I have been to school for eight years. I don't speak Serbian. I recognise some letters in Cyrillic. We learned a little bit of it in year four, when I was in year four. I can remember some of the basic words such as good afternoon, good evening, and so on, but not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So regarding number 7 on that page of P327, are you recognising the letters or are you recognising the word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, I'm only recognising the Cyrillic letters. This -- only this I know, but I don't know how to read or to understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, number 7 -- or, excuse me, number 6 right next to it is similar, not knowing much Cyrillic myself. Could it have potentially been those letters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Really, I don't remember. You can imagine the situation I was in. I couldn't lift my head and look at them closely. I only know that there was a writing on their arms and that the writing was in Cyrillic letters. I had seven children to look after from six months to 12 years, so they were all around me and that was the only concern I had at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So, ma'am, is it your testimony today that they had an insignia on them with Cyrillic letters, but you don't know what it said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I am repeating, I don't know what the word meant. I only know that the letters were Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Did you see these uniforms you've just described in Drenovac as well or just in Beleg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Only in Beleg. In Drenoc we didn't have any contacts with the police - we women I mean - only men had.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you left Drenoc, you said in your testimony previously it's because the police told the men to leave, so then the whole village left. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The men went out in the street and they told us that the police had ordered them to leave Drenoc. That's how it came that all of us with tractors, whatever we had, left the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Which men told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The men of the village, of Drenoc village, those men who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you see the conversation with the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, I didn't see the men talking with the police, but the men came to us, to us women and children, telling us to leave the village. And that's how we acted, that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, we'll be careful to protect your identity not to mention any relationships. If you want to, we can go into private session. But was Mehmet Mazrekaj someone who had told you about this conversation with the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were many men from the village. Mehmet was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And did the police tell the men to leave due to expected NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I don't know that. I only know that the men said to us to leave the village because the police had told them to do so. This I know from the men who came to us, and we, all of us, as you know, left the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But no one ever told you why you were leaving the village or what the police had said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, I don't know what the police told the men, but I do know that we left the village and went to Beleg. When we went to Beleg, Drenoc village was burned. We saw the flames coming out of the houses of Drenoc.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you know that Mehmet Mazrekaj was a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you follow his testimony or hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If he gave an answer that said that: "That day the police arrived at around 8.00 in the morning. Some -- they expelled some villagers and they ordered us to vacate the village as soon as we possibly could because of NATO air-strikes they said." Would you believe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I don't know what he said here. I'm telling you what I saw and what I heard. I don't know what other people may have said here. Mehmet didn't say this to me. I never heard him say such words.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay, ma'am. So from that time, you left Drenoc and went on to Beleg. How did you come to stay at the home of Naim Vishaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The population of the village, of Beleg, came out and they took us to their houses. So our population spread out in the village. My turn came with my children to go to Naim's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know how Naim's house was selected as the place to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: This is how it came. My turn came to go to that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say your turn came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: We stayed at Naim's house. There was nowhere else I could go. He was someone I knew. I recognised him from before, an acquaintance of mine. As I said, the population spread out in different houses. It was not only myself. There were other families that went to Naim's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you said there were approximately a hundred people at Naim's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was not only myself and my children. There were many other families from Drenoc, from Beleg. There were several families. I could say that we were approximately 100 persons accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you and your husband and your children were actually from Glodjane; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were there other --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. We are from Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And were there other families from Glodjane at Naim's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, only myself and my children.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, you said today that you stayed in the house, you said this in prior testimony as well, that there was shelling, constant shelling going on. Approximately what day was this, the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: On the 27th of March, I think, or the 28th. I cannot be 100 per cent sure of the exact date. I only know that shelling went on all along the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this shelling, do you know, was it in-fighting between the KLA and Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that there was a lot of shelling, so much so that we couldn't dare to go out in the yard. Shelling came from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And you said that the next day the police came to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. It was about 9.00 when the police came and entered.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you say "entered," they entered into the yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you say they first asked about the number of displaced families in the house and where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They called the host, Naim, and asked him, Who is staying with you? He said, I have people from Beleg and Drenoc. The police asked him, Is it true that people are -- that these people are here from these villages? He said, Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you've stated, ma'am, that you don't understand Serbian. Was the officer speaking Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No. Naim spoke with them. When Naim came back to us, I heard him saying that, It's true that these people are from Beleg and Drenoc. Now I don't remember exactly whether Naim said this or whether I heard it. This I have forgotten. And they took the men out and lined them up. It took them out of that room and ordered them to go out into the yard, and there they lined them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, I want to go back just a few seconds. Earlier today you said they "forced Naim to order all of us to leave." Did Naim tell you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The police had told Naim to take all the men out in the yard. Naim came in and told the men to go out. The police looked at the men and then they let them go, and then the men came back to the house. On the next day, they came again and entered and they forced us to leave the house, to go outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, we'll get to the next day, but I want to finish with this conversation quickly that happened on that morning. You state in your statement you were scared because you were from Gllogjan and the UCK headquarters was in the village of Gllogjan and you told your husband to say he was not from Gllogjan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I told my husband that the police had told Naim so and so, and Naim had told the police that people are from Drenoc and Beleg. Being from Gllogjan, I was afraid for my husband, telling him when he went outside not to say that he was from Gllogjan because afraid that something bad might happen to Naim for not having told the police that my husband was from Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In your testimony you stated something similar at T7472 you said: "I told my husband to tell Naim that he was from Drenoc for Naim not to have problems with the police ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I said to my husband, Say you are from Drenoc, not from Gllogjan. Now I don't remember whether I told Naim or my husband, but I remember very well that I told him to deny that he was from Gllogjan, not to mention Gllogjan, but to say he was from Drenoc.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, why did you tell him not to mention he was from Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I said this because I was afraid the police might cause some harm to Naim, because Naim didn't mention Gllogjan. And I didn't want any harm to come to this person, to Naim. That's why I was afraid they would do something bad to Naim if he -- if they found out that we were from Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, why would it be bad if you were from Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Because in Gllogjan there were KLA and I was afraid Naim would suffer something if they found out we were from Gllogjan. The KLA headquarters were in Gllogjan, and I didn't want to cause any harm to Naim, even though we were all civilians as I said. We had nothing to do with the KLA, but I was still -- I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it was your belief initially that the police were there to look for UCK; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, no, no. There was no reason for them to do that because there was no KLA there. The KLA was in Gllogjan. I was only afraid that being from Gllogjan and having Naim accommodating us in his home, I was afraid something might happen to him. As I told you earlier, we were all civilians, men, women, children, elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm not saying that your husband or anyone was in the KLA, actually. What I'm saying is that you were telling your husband to say he was not from Glodjane because you were afraid that the police were looking for KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, I told my husband, Don't say you are from Gllogjan because Naim told the police that the people in my house are only from Beleg and Drenoc. And since my husband was from Gllogjan and given that Naim didn't mention it, I asked my husband not to mention Gllogjan. What else can I say? How best can I explain to you? I'm telling you, I didn't want Naim to suffer because of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, how many men were in the house at that time when the police came that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: To -- what can I say? I don't know exactly -- the exact number. There were about 20, I would say about 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you say that they returned the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The police came back on the next day and entered Naim's house at about 9.00 in the morning, and they forced all of us to leave the house and go outside in the yard. And they started shooting and killing us. The first one was Naim -- Nezir Vishaj, and they killed him -- I think they shot him on his cheek. The second one was Daut Alickaj. He too was killed. He fell on the ground immediately. I saw that with my own eyes. We came out as we were, without properly dressed. Some were not having -- wearing shoes, some were -- as we were staying in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, was it Naim or Nezir who was shot in the cheek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Nezir was shot by the police when he was going out at the entrance, at the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you mentioned today that you had heard from Naim's wife that she heard shots from the shed, I believe it was, after Naim had been taken that direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They took Naim afterwards. Wait a little, I'll explain to you. We all went out. First Nezir Vishaj, they shot him and killed him. Then the second one was Daut Alickaj, he too was killed on the spot. Then they took Naim, and this I saw with my own eyes, took him in the direction of the shed. They killed him, but I didn't see him being killed. I only heard his wife saying that Naim was killed and that she had heard the shots, but I didn't see the exact moment that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did his wife see the moment that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No, no. She only heard the shots, the fire-arms, and that she thought he was dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at this point then, the rest of you are taken to another house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They took us to another house in another basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you had mentioned today about some people - and it was plural - being paralyzed. I had understood previously only one woman as being paralyzed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There was a woman who was paralyzed, she was staying at Naim's house, and she couldn't walk. When we were forced to go to this other house, to this basement, they beat this woman. Her daughters told the police that she's paralyzed and cannot walk. This woman I knew that she was paralyzed. I don't know about the others because I couldn't -- didn't check. But this woman I saw and I knew that she was paralyzed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was Nezir Vishaj's wife; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, she was the wife of Nezir Vishaj, this paralyzed woman, the one who couldn't walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, there was some conflicting accounts between your previous -- your statement and your testimony about the white cloth that was put out and whether you were the first person there or the first person in your group. But I think that you somehow resolved that now in correcting your statement. And in the note that we got you stated: "When she was taken to the basement the witness saw that on the white piece of cloth there were all the valuables from people who were checked before her ..." That's correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But now you've actually added that there were ID cards on this sheet too; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I didn't change anything. I simply remembered one more detail, because I simply added there -- I haven't changed anything. I remembered this now. I remember that there were IDs. There was money, there were valuables, but it's not that I have changed or altered anything. And you know, it may happen that one forgets something when you recount such horrible stories, but then you may remember it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But that's what I want to make sure. You didn't remember the ID cards in 2000 or 2004 or 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I didn't remember because I was shocked. Even now to this day I don't feel completely restored. We are still undergoing therapy. I have problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I understand, ma'am, and I do appreciate you recalling the best of your recollection, but I'm just asking why the ID cards suddenly came to you now, this time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Because I remembered when I entered there, the basement, I saw the IDs. And I heard some say that, They took away our IDs. So when I entered the basement I saw that on that piece of cloth, on that white piece of cloth, those IDs and then I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But would you say your memory is better --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: And when we were going to Albania --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, would you say your memory is better now or back when you gave the initial statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I remember very well that there were IDs, and I know that when we were going towards Albania the police stopped us and asked us to hand over the IDs. And we told the police that we don't have them, that they were taken away from us in that basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, you've said today that you gave away your jewellery and money before -- well, you've said prior that it was before they asked you, and today you said the words of your free will. Is that correct that you saw the white sheet on the floor and you put your items on that white sheet without being asked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes. When I entered, I told you that there were four of us. I was the first of the four women who entered. And once I entered and when I saw the things I mentioned in the -- on that piece of cloth, I handed over of my own free will what I had on me. And they said, You go now. And then I left behind those three other ladies. I was afraid they would have searched me and I didn't want that. That's why I surrendered everything I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But nobody --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They checked -- they searched even my children.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, no one ever said, Give us what you have from money and jewels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: No one said, but I knew since they asked us to go down to the basement -- there was a reason for that. I saw the things lying on that piece of sheet. That's why I didn't want them to search me and that's why I handed over whatever I had to them myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. But I'm wondering why then under oath you were asked, Did you do this all of your own accord? And you said: "No, no, no. They said, 'Give us what you have from money and jewels -- jewellery.'" And that was in your Milutinovic testimony. Why did you say that then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Let me explain to you. Please don't ask me the same questions over and over again. I will explain. I entered there with a group of four or five. I was obliged to give them what I had because that's why they asked us to go down to the basement. I simply didn't wait them to search me because I was scared, and I handed over whatever I had. I didn't want to have them -- I wanted to be done with it. I wanted to go back to my children. And please, please don't ask me the same questions. I was really scared. And even now when I remember them, I'm not in a very good position to give you an answer. So please don't ask me again. I don't feel very well, and I think I will lose control of my emotions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, I think we're nearing a break and maybe this would be a good time, Your Honour, then if we take a break you could rest for a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What we will do now is have an interruption of the questioning. That will give you an opportunity to have a drink and rest a little, and we will resume in half an hour. The time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but please, I would kindly ask you, Your Honour, to use your power and not let the lady ask me over and over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The lady is trying to understand clearly what it is that you are describing. Sometimes your answers are not altogether clear; that's why she asks you a second time. If you can try and understand that and help us by trying to make your answers clear. But have a break now, and we will resume --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you then. And we'll return in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We hope you're feeling a little better now. Thank you. Now Ms. O'Leary will just finish her questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. We'll try to be as short as possible so we don't have to stay too much longer. I understood that nothing was said to you today. What I was asking you actually was why in a passage from T7488 to T7490 in Milutinovic there was the exchange where you actually said that they were speaking to you in Serbian. What I'm wondering is: Did anyone at any time speak to you in Serbian there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness. Could the witness be asked to repeat the answer because we could not hear most of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we've only just connected to you so that we missed what you were saying at the beginning. Would you mind repeating that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me about where we were taken to be searched?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you put your items on the white sheet, did anyone speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Before I went there to be searched, I asked the women that had been there earlier and -- what had happened to them, and they told me that they had been searched and everything that they had had been taken away from them. So when my turn came to go with the other women, I did not wait for them to tell me to give them the things or to let them search me. I just gave them all the things I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that, ma'am. So after you put your things on the white cloth, you were not searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I was not searched because I handed over everything I had. As I told you, my friends had -- the other women had told me earlier that they had been searched. So when my turn came, I went there first, I was in first. And I just gave them everything because I wanted out of there to go to my children immediately. When I went back to my children, they came there and searched my children.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, the items that were put on the white cloth were returned the next day by a policeman; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Golden things were returned. They brought some of the jewellery there, golden things, and they said, Whose are these things here? And the women went there and took each of them what was theirs.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was a policeman; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: He was a policeman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then that evening you describe there were girls being taken out of the room, and the room that you were in was on the ground level or in the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: It was on the ground level. It was like a hallway or a living-room, I would say, of that family home.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it was evening and it was dark; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, don't say any names right away --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: We were told to go to two different rooms. We were divided into two. Some of us were taken to this room I mentioned. The others were taken to the shed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Without saying any names right away, would you be able to name any of the girls who were taken out if we went into private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I didn't know them --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- none of them --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- they all were new to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And you said the men coming in needed torches, so they were shining with flash-lights. It was probably difficult to see anything behind them; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Because there was no power, they came in with their torches and they asked for the young girls to come out because they needed them for cleaning.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you had initially in your statement at page 7 had described this as two paramilitaries, and I believe in your transcript of testimony prior you also said at T7476 there was one by the door and one looking at the girls. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. One of them was at the door and the other one came inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you even named one of them in your statement as Mushk Jakupi's son; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. I recognised Mushk Jakupi's son the third time they came when the torch light fell on his face, that's when I recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What ethnicity is Mushk Jakupi's son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I don't know him. I have heard that he's Albanian. I didn't know him personally. I heard this from other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Who did you hear that from, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I heard this from the men. They mentioned his name, and they said that he was committing crimes. I heard people say that Mushk Jakupi's son was committing crimes, but I didn't know him. In Gjakova he was committing those crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned that on October 10th, 2006, we have a proofing note where you were speaking with the Office of the Prosecutor and you stated the son of Mushk Jakupi is mentioned on pages 5 and 6, referring to your statement, Mushk Jakupi is known by his bad reputation in the region. He is a police officer. The son was paramilitary. Did you mean that his son had a bad reputation or he had a bad reputation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I had heard this about both of them. This is all things I heard from other people, though, as I said. Everybody was saying that Mushk Jakupi's son was doing those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what was he wearing when you saw him, when the light passed by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Camouflage, green camouflage uniforms -- uniform, the same clothes he was wearing when he was on the tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And did you consider him then to be police or paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: To be honest, I just saw him wearing those clothes, that kind of uniform, and I told you what I was told by my husband. I don't know further than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, the reason I ask is because you have referred to him as being paramilitary twice now, once in your statement when you're discussing the people who came to take the girls out as paramilitary, and then in that proofing note as the son was paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: He had green camouflage uniform. The police had solid blue uniforms. And I just assumed that the people who were wearing that other kind of uniform were paramilitaries. And this is only my assumption, approximate assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, also in the -- in regards to the sexual assault and taking the girls out of there, you had made a note in this note of 2006 where you said: "While the paramilitaries were the ones soliciting the girls, the following day the police were still in the village ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. I heard the girl with my own eyes -- with my own ears.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat the question, please. I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Sure. I was quoting actually from a note taken in your proofing statement of 2006 that says: "While the paramilitaries were the ones soliciting the girls, the following day the police were still in the village ..." But that sentence would indicate pretty clearly that it was paramilitaries taking the girls out that night. Was that your intention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I recognised Mushk Jakupi's son only once. And I don't know about the other times. I couldn't tell you whether they were policemen or paramilitary because I couldn't see their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And I believe that's what you say now in the note that was taken this last week is that it was dark and you couldn't -- you said: "The witness could see Mushk Jakupi's son only one of the times he went into the room to pick up the young girls. She was able to see and recognise him because of the flash of light ..." You also say: "She does not remember very well, and it was dark in the room."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: That's correct. It was dark, that's true, it was dark. But the flash-light just passed on his face when he was looking for the girls, and that's when I recognised him. The other times, I don't know whether he was there or not. I couldn't recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in your prior testimony at 7477 you said: "We could not raise our eyes to see who they were. We were very afraid. However, I know that they entered, they came in, and they took the girls away ..." So you did not see the girls being taken away by the men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I saw the girls being taken away from that room. They left the room, but I couldn't see who took them. They were taken out of there by force, and they were telling them, You have to come to do some cleaning work.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you didn't have opportunity to see who the people were taking the girls out of the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question again. I couldn't hear it very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I just wanted to confirm that you couldn't identify who took the girls out of the room then, other than seeing Mushk Jakupi's son at one point; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I couldn't identify any of them, whether they were policemen or paramilitaries, because it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And the next day you stated in your statement that two paramilitaries came and told you to leave. And this was on page 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: The next day, two of them came in and they told us to leave the place and go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you used the word "paramilitaries" in your statement; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: They were paramilitaries because they had green camouflage uniforms. As I said, I assumed they were paramilitaries. I don't know what else they could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And when you left then, do you remember the route that you took to Kukes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. We went from Beleg to Carrabreg, and then Rastovice, Hereq, Gjakove, Zhur, and then to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And had you been --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: We were stopped several times en route.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you took that route because you were escorted by the police; is that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I did not see them because I was on a lorry and I couldn't see outside. There were so many of us on that lorry, but I heard the men say that they are escorting us. I did not see them with my own eyes, however, because the lorry was packed full and it was covered so I couldn't see anything. I heard the men say that we were being escorted.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You heard that you were being escorted by the police, but did you see the paramilitary groups that stopped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: En route -- no, I couldn't see them from the lorry because, as I told you, the lorry was covered and we couldn't see outside. Only the driver spoke with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay, ma'am. But you discussed just a few moments ago that the paramilitaries were stopping you along the way to check identification; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I did not see them. I don't know. I just heard of this. The convoy was stopped several times, but whether it was stopped by the police or the paramilitaries, I don't know. It was the driver who communicated with them all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I think we're supposed to take one pause here quickly to get the transcript fixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will pause a moment if your transcript has gone as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: It has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll be able to start again very shortly. Sorry to keep you waiting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Your Honour. I can wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a technician working on the problem at the moment. It's apparently affected our whole building, so we'll just have to wait a little longer. Sorry about that. We're able to recommence I believe, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We were just discussing sort of the route you took to Kukes and what had happened along the way, and you stated that you did not see the police but you heard they were escorting you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I heard --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: -- I heard people saying that, They are escorting us. But I can't tell you how far they escorted us.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's okay, ma'am. I just wanted to make sure that I had that correctly before we took the pause. Because you also said that you had heard that the paramilitaries were stopping. But am I correct that you never saw the paramilitaries along the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K58
utterances.text: I didn't see them with my own eyes because, as I said, we were on top of a truck and the truck was covered with this tarpaulin. And so only the driver talked with them.
